explanation: I found no Mathlib lemma that gives this result directly or in one or two short steps. Every mention of `expMeasure` in Mathlib is in `Probability/Distributions/Exponential.lean`. That file defines `expMeasure` and proves `isProbabilityMeasure_expMeasure` and some CDF lemmas (`cdf_expMeasure_eq`, `cdf_expMeasure_eq_integral`, `cdf_expMeasure_eq_lintegral`). Nothing there or elsewhere in Mathlib gives the measure of `Ici t`, i.e. the tail exp(-t). Getting the tail from `cdf_expMeasure_eq` takes several steps: take complements, show the measure has no atoms (so `Ici` and `Ioi` have the same measure), and pass between ENNReal and real values. That is more than one or two lines of routine glue. The library's proof uses its own lemma `ExponentialTransfer.expMeasure_one_Ici`, which is not part of Mathlib.
